entities.name: Giacomo Colonna
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Giacomo Colonna (died August 14, 1318) was a prominent Italian cardinal and a leading figure in the powerful Colonna family, whose political and military influence profoundly shaped the tumultuous landscape of late 13th and early 14th-century Rome and the Papal States. His life was inextricably linked to the fierce power struggles between the Roman nobility and the papacy, particularly his direct and defiant opposition to Pope Boniface VIII, which escalated into one of the most significant ecclesiastical and political conflicts of the Medieval era. This protracted feud, driven by ambition and theological disputes, fundamentally challenged papal supremacy and contributed to the weakening of the papacy's temporal power, directly preceding the Avignon Papacy.

Appointed cardinal-deacon in 1278 by Pope Nicholas III, Giacomo initially held significant ecclesiastical power, but his career was irrevocably defined by his conflict with Boniface VIII, who ascended to the papacy in 1294. The Colonna family, including Giacomo and his nephew Pietro, openly questioned the legitimacy of Boniface's election, alleging his predecessor Celestine V's resignation was invalid. This challenge culminated in the 'Manifesto of Lunghezza' in 1297, in which Giacomo and Pietro publicly denounced Boniface as an illegitimate pope and a heretic. In response, Boniface excommunicated the Colonna cardinals, declared a crusade against the family, confiscated their vast estates, and ordered the destruction of their strongholds, including Palestrina.
